records.name: Community Schools @Alexander K. McClure School
records.summary: Alexander K. McClure is one of the City's Community Schools for pre-K through fifth grade. Volunteers can help with programs for students and families, including weekly reading coaching.
records.what_you_do: Coach students in reading each week, or help with school programs for students and families when shifts are posted.

schedule.text: Weekly reading coach shifts, posted on the city's volunteer portal.

locations.label: School
locations.address: 600 W Hunting Park Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19140

access.notes: Accommodation requests can be sent through a form on the school's website. The school page describes no physical access features.

first_step.how: Sign up for a posted reading coach shift on the city's volunteer portal, or email commschools@phila.gov to ask about the next opening.
first_step.basis: The city lists this volunteer role publicly with a sign-up step. The school page does not say which clearances apply, so paperwork may come first.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers work inside the school, and the school's Community School Coordinator arranges the programs. Reading coaching is a weekly role, according to the city listing. The school page does not give shift times, how long a shift runs, or any clearance steps, so ask before you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Ask the coordinator which entrance to use and where to check in.
Ask which clearances you need before you sign up for a shift.

records.notes: Galaxydigital volunteer listing returned HTTP 403 to this run, so the reading coach role and weekly shift are carried from tier 1 and not re-verified. The school site lists a monthly community gathering dated December 17, 2025, which sets the status and last sign of life. Tier 1 last_sign_of_life (2026-10) rested on the listing's seen date, not a written date, so it was corrected. The school main line is (215) 400-3870; the volunteer contact above is the one from the city listing.

records.name: Community Schools @Murrell Dobbins CTE High School
records.summary: Murrell Dobbins is a career and technical high school for grades 9 to 12 and one of the City's Community Schools. Volunteers help with the school's food distribution, its pantries, and events such as resource fairs.
records.what_you_do: Hand out groceries each week to students and families, help run the food and clothing pantries, and help at school events.

schedule.text: Weekly grocery distribution to students and families, according to the city volunteer listing.

access.notes: The school site links an accommodations page and an accessibility notice but describes no physical access features.

first_step.how: Call the school at (215) 400-7050 and ask the Community School Coordinator about the next grocery or pantry shift, and which clearances to complete first.
first_step.basis: Volunteers need district and state clearances and a city release form before a first shift, and the school site does not explain how to start. The way in takes paperwork and a call to the coordinator.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect a paperwork step before your first shift, since the volunteer listing asks for district and state clearances and a city release form. Shifts involve handing out groceries each week, working the food and clothing pantries, and helping at events such as resource fairs. Neither the school site nor the city page gives shift length, so ask the coordinator.
first_visit_tips: Ask the coordinator which entrance to use and where to check in.
Ask early which clearances must be finished before your first shift.

records.notes: Galaxydigital volunteer listing returned HTTP 403 to this run, so the clearance requirements, grocery and pantry roles, and the weekly grocery schedule are carried from tier 1 and not re-verified. The school site has no volunteer details. The city page lists Fresh For All produce stand dates at this school on October 14 and October 21, 2026, run with Philabundance. That is a public food event rather than a volunteer shift, so it is not in schedule. The school site shows grades 9 to 12 and main line (215) 400-7050.

records.name: Community Schools @Richard R. Wright
records.summary: Richard R. Wright School is one of the City's Community Schools. Volunteers help hand out groceries, work the on-site food pantry, and support school events such as resource fairs.
records.what_you_do: Help hand out weekly groceries to students and families, work the on-site food pantry, and help at school events.

schedule.text: Weekly grocery distribution to students and families, according to the city volunteer listing.

access.notes: Translation and accessibility accommodations can be requested for school events through the district's accommodations form.

first_step.how: Use the district volunteer sign-up linked from the school site, or call (215) 400-7030 to ask the Community School Coordinator about the next grocery or pantry shift.
first_step.basis: The school invites families to volunteer and links to the district form, but the volunteer listing asks for clearances and a city release before a first shift, so the way in takes paperwork.
first_step.what_to_expect: The school site invites families to volunteer and links to the district's sign-up page. The volunteer listing asks for district and state clearances and a city release form, so plan for paperwork before a first shift. Shifts cover weekly groceries, the on-site food pantry, and school events, and neither source gives shift length.
first_visit_tips: Ask the school which clearances you need before the first shift.
Call the school to ask where to check in on your first day.

records.notes: Galaxydigital volunteer listing returned HTTP 403 to this run, so the clearance requirements and the grocery and pantry roles are carried from tier 1 and not re-verified. The school site shows 'Last modified: August 11, 2026'. That is a page date, not a news item, so status is probably_active rather than active; its one award post carries no date on the page. Tier 1 last_sign_of_life (2026-10) was replaced with 2026-08. Main line (215) 400-7030; the Instagram account is the school's own.

records.name: Community Schools @William Cramp Elementary School
records.summary: William Cramp Elementary is one of the City's Community Schools for kindergarten through fifth grade. Volunteers are sometimes needed for grocery giveaways and special events.
records.what_you_do: Help now and then at grocery giveaways and special events, when the school asks for volunteers.

first_step.how: Call the school at (215) 400-3860 and ask the Community School Coordinator how volunteers sign up for the next grocery giveaway or event.
first_step.basis: The school site does not describe volunteer sign-up, and the city listing is the only route found, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Neither the school site nor the city page describes volunteer shifts or clearances. The city listing says volunteers are needed now and then for grocery giveaways and special events. Ask the coordinator how long each event runs and what paperwork applies before you come.
first_visit_tips: Call ahead, since the school site lists no volunteer sign-up steps.
Ask which clearances apply before you agree to help.

records.notes: The school site has no dated items (its news posts carry no dates) and no volunteer details, so status is probably_active as a working site with no dates. Tier 1 last_sign_of_life (2026-10) rested on the listing's seen date and was removed. Galaxydigital listing returned HTTP 403 to this run; the occasional grocery giveaway role is carried from tier 1 and not re-verified. The school posts a parent engagement survey in English and Spanish, with no deadline shown.

records.name: HACE CDC
records.summary: HACE CDC is the registered community organization for part of Fairhill and St. Hugh. It holds public virtual meetings where residents hear about development projects that need zoning changes, and they can weigh in before the city decides.
records.what_you_do: Go to the virtual community meetings, ask questions about zoning and development plans, and share your view. The group sends a summary letter to the city before the Zoning Board of Adjustment hearing.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: Virtual meeting by Zoom; email smonteiro@hacecdc.org to register

locations.label: Main office
locations.address: 167 W. Allegheny Avenue, Suite 200, Philadelphia, PA 19140

first_step.how: Email Stasia Monteiro at smonteiro@hacecdc.org to register for the next virtual community meeting.
first_step.basis: Community meetings are open to residents, and the page gives one clear way in, which is to contact the program director. The page does not say who can become a member.
first_step.what_to_expect: A first visit is a virtual meeting where a project is presented and residents discuss it. The page describes a set order: a preliminary meeting with the applicant, a community meeting, a committee vote, then a summary letter to the city. It does not say how long meetings run or whether anything costs money.
first_visit_tips: Email the program director first to get the meeting link and the date.
Test your audio and camera before the call starts.

records.notes: The HACE news archive runs only to April 2022 and the events calendar showed no entries. The newest dated items are on the homepage and all come from 2025 (a monthly summer event that began June 13, 2025), so status is probably_active. Virtual meeting dates and the Zoom link are not published; email to the program director is the only listed route. The site never spells out the Hispanic Association name, so the link to the duplicate record rests on shared office, phone and staff, plus HACE's own homepage listing a Neighborhood Advisory Committee as one of its programs. The homepage names Maria N. Gonzalez as president and CEO.

records.name: Hunting Park Neighborhood Advisory Committee
records.summary: A neighborhood committee and nonprofit for the Hunting Park area. It helps residents with utility bill grants, energy savings, repairs, and emergency food, and it holds community meetings on zoning.
records.what_you_do: Residents come to the office for help with utility bills, energy use, repairs, or emergency food. The group also works on housing, education, jobs, beautification, and recreation.

first_step.how: Call the office at (215) 225-5560 to ask about the next community meeting or to ask for help with a utility bill.
first_step.basis: The site gives a phone number and an address but no meeting dates, sign-up steps, or email, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The website does not describe a first visit. It describes utility, energy, and repair help for low-income residents, and says community meetings are held, without giving dates or a place. Call the office to find out what a meeting covers and what to bring for a request.
first_visit_tips: Call ahead, since the site lists no office hours or meeting dates.
Ask the office what papers to bring for a grant or repair request.

records.notes: The newest dated item on the group's site is a newsletter dated March 2015. The footer reads copyright 2015, which is not evidence of activity. An undated food notice says 'In September!' with no year. The city NAC list still names the group, but a listing is not dated activity, so status is dormant. A web search for 2026 meetings found nothing, and the /news/ page returned HTTP 404. Tier 1 name read 'Hunting Park Community Revitilization Corporation'; the group's own site calls itself the Hunting Park Neighborhood Advisory Committee (HPNAC), so the display name follows the site. The email comes from the city list only; the site lists none. Tier 1 last_sign_of_life (2026-10) was replaced because no written 2026 date was found. The owner may want to confirm the group is still active before it goes live.
